box-all: Boxy + Mismatch: every rectangle is used

Every piece is a different rectangle, and the board has exactly as many tiles as all the rectangles still possible put together. So each of those rectangles is used once, and each needs a place on the board.
gd-clash: Gemini and Delta: never the same two pieces
A Gemini wall has two pieces of the same shape on its sides and a Delta wall two pieces of different shapes, so a Gemini wall and a Delta wall are always between different pairs of pieces.
mingle-area-place: Size Separation: a place for the piece
Touching pieces always have different sizes. This piece has a known size, and the solver listed every place it can take where it touches no other piece of that size. They all agree on this edge.
hetero-place: Heterogeneous: a place for the piece

With Heterogeneous, touching pieces always have different sizes. This piece has a known size, and the solver listed every place it can take where it touches no other piece of that size. They all agree on this edge.
area-place: Area number: every place the piece fits
The solver listed every place where the piece of this area number still fits with its size. They all agree on this edge.
mingle-area-single: Size Separation: one size for every piece
Only one size is possible, and touching pieces always have different sizes, so no two pieces touch: every edge left is open.
mingle-shape-single: Mingle Shape: one shape for every piece
Only one shape is possible, and touching pieces always have different shapes, so no two pieces touch: every edge left is open.
hetero-single: Heterogeneous: one size for every piece
Only one size is possible, and with Heterogeneous touching pieces always have different sizes, so no two pieces touch: every edge left is open.
mingle-area-corner: Size Separation: never three walls at a corner

Only two sizes are possible and touching pieces have different sizes, so three pieces never meet at one corner: a corner never has exactly three walls. The walls already at this corner leave one choice.
mingle-shape-corner: Mingle Shape: never three walls at a corner

Only two shapes are possible and touching pieces have different shapes, so three pieces never meet at one corner: a corner never has exactly three walls. The walls already at this corner leave one choice.
hetero-corner: Heterogeneous: never three walls at a corner

Only two sizes are possible and with Heterogeneous touching pieces have different sizes, so three pieces never meet at one corner: a corner never has exactly three walls. The walls already at this corner leave one choice.

stamp-place: Stamp: every place the shape fits
The solver listed every place where the stamp's shape still fits. Edges outside all of them are walls; edges inside all of them are open.

bank-place: Shape bank: every place a shape fits
The solver listed every placement of every bank shape (all turns and flips) that still fits around this group. Edges outside all of them are walls; edges inside all of them are open.

bridge-count: The board is held together here by a single connection, and only one choice for it leaves each side with a number of tiles whole pieces of the allowed sizes can cover.
The board is held together here by a single connection. With one piece crossing it, the tiles left on each side could only be covered by pieces of sizes the rules forbid. So it is a wall.

The board is held together here by a single connection. With a wall here, each side would need to be covered by whole pieces on its own, and its number of tiles makes that impossible. So one piece crosses it: the two tiles are in one piece.

The two pieces of a Gemini wall have the same shape, so a straight line in one has a twin of the same length in the other. The solver checked every place where the twin could still have a line that long, and the lengths left say where this line ends.

gemini-anchor: Gemini: the one line that can match

Both pieces of the Gemini wall have a closed straight line of the same length, and one of them has room for only that one. So the turn or mirror that copies one shape onto the other sends line onto line. Of those few ways, the ones that still fit after copying the known tiles across all agree on these edges.
